arxiv-1802-08375.title: Reusing Weights in Subword-aware Neural Language Models
arxiv-1802-08375.creator: Zhenisbek Assylbekov, Rustem Takhanov
arxiv-1802-08375.description: Abstract We propose several ways of reusing subword embeddings and other weights in subword-aware neural language models. The proposed techniques do not benefit a competitive character-aware model, but some of them improve the performance of syllable- and morpheme-aware models while showing significant reductions in model sizes.

arxiv-2010-14868.title: Bipartite quantum measurements with optimal single-sided distinguishability
arxiv-2010-14868.creator: Jakub Czartowski, Karol Życzkowski
arxiv-2010-14868.description: Abstract We analyse orthogonal bases in a composite N × N N\times N Hilbert space describing a bipartite quantum system and look for a basis with optimal single-sided mutual state distinguishability. This condition implies that in each subsystem the N 2 N^{2} reduced states form a regular simplex of a maximal edge length, defined with respect to the trace distance.

arxiv-2109-09003.title: Inertial domain wall characterization in layered multisublattice antiferromagnets
arxiv-2109-09003.creator: R. Rama-Eiroa, P. E. Roy, J. M. González, K. Y. Guslienko, J. Wunderlich, R. M. Otxoa
arxiv-2109-09003.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by R. Rama-Eiroa, P. E. Roy, J. M. González, K. Y. Guslienko, J. Wunderlich, R. M. Otxoa. The motion of a Néel-like 180 ∘ {180}^{\circ} domain wall induced by a time-dependent staggered spin-orbit field in the layered collinear antiferromagnet Mn 2 Au is explored.

arxiv-2112-02550.title: Valley and Valley-like Split-ring Topological Photonic Crystal
arxiv-2112-02550.creator: Hui-Chang Li, Chen Luo, Tai-Lin Zhang, Jian-Wei Xu, Xiang Zhou, Yun Shen, Xiao-Hua Deng
arxiv-2112-02550.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Hui-Chang Li, Chen Luo, Tai-Lin Zhang, Jian-Wei Xu, Xiang Zhou, Yun Shen, Xiao-Hua Deng. In the research of topological phases of matter, valley pseudospins have been introduced into photonic systems. Here, we construct a split-ring photonic crystal (SPC) in which the spilt rings are distributed according to the Kagome model.

arxiv-2307-14841.title: On the Suitability of Hugging Face Hub for Empirical Studies
arxiv-2307-14841.creator: Adem Ait, Javier Luis Cánovas Izquierdo, Jordi Cabot
arxiv-2307-14841.description: Abstract Background. The development of empirical studies in software engineering mainly relies on the data available on code hosting platforms, being GitHub the most representative. Nevertheless, in the last years, the emergence of Machine Learning (ML) has led to the development of platforms specifically designed for developing ML-based projects, being Hugging Face Hub (HFH) the most popular one.

arxiv-2312-06866.title: Probing Disk Ice Content and PAH Emission Through Multiband MagAO+Clio Images of HD 141569
arxiv-2312-06866.creator: Jay K. Kueny, Alycia J. Weinberger, Jared R. Males, Katie M. Morzinski, Laird M. Close, Katherine B. Follette, Philip M. Hinz
arxiv-2312-06866.description: Abstract We present resolved images of the inner disk component around HD 141569A using the Magellan adaptive optics system with the Clio2 1 - 5 ​ μ 5\mu m camera, offering a glimpse of a complex system thought to be in a short evolutionary phase between protoplanetary and debris disk stages.

arxiv-2408-17417.title: Magnetic and crystal electric field studies in the rare-earth-based square lattice antiferromagnet NdKNaNbO 5
arxiv-2408-17417.creator: S. Guchhait, A. Painganoor, S. S. Islam, J. Sichelschmidt, M. D. Le, N. B. Christensen, R. Nath
arxiv-2408-17417.description: Abstract The interplay of magnetic correlations, crystal electric field interactions, and spin-orbit coupling in low-dimensional frustrated magnets fosters novel ground states with unusual excitations. Here, we report the magnetic properties and crystal electric field (CEF) scheme of a rare-earth-based square-lattice antiferromagnet NdKNaNbO 5 investigated via magnetization, specific heat, electron spin resonance (ESR), and inelastic neutron scattering (INS) experiments.

arxiv-2410-08124.title: The cohomological equation and cyclic cocycles for renormalizable minimal Cantor systems
arxiv-2410-08124.creator: Rodrigo Treviño
arxiv-2410-08124.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Rodrigo Treviño. For typical properly ordered and minimal Bratteli diagrams ( B , ≤ r ) (B,\leq_{r}) , it is shown that there are finitely many invariant distributions 𝒟 i \mathcal{D}_{i} which are the only obstructions to solving the cohomological equation f = u − u ∘ ϕ f=u-u\circ\phi for the corresponding adic transformation ϕ : X B → X B \phi:X_{B}\rightarrow X_{B} and for α \alpha -Hölder f f with α \alpha large enough.

arxiv-2507-00820.title: Deducing the Talbot Effect from Electrodynamics
arxiv-2507-00820.creator: Gabriel Ybarra Marcaida
arxiv-2507-00820.description:
A 2025 arXiv research paper by Gabriel Ybarra Marcaida. Abstract

We propose a model based on Maxwell’s equations to describe the Talbot effect. After solving the model analytically, we prove that its solution is equivalent to the one amply found in the literature in the asymptotic limit. By considering the paraxial limit, we showcase how the rational Talbot effect arises, and derive an ideal paraxial distribution that would give such effects. We give a proof of
L^{2}
-convergence to these ideal distributions for any such grating.

arxiv-2509-07588.creator: Andrey Sakhovskiy, Elena Tutubalina
arxiv-2509-07588.description: Abstract . In recent years, there has been substantial progress in using pretrained Language Models (LMs) on a range of tasks aimed at improving the understanding of biomedical texts. Nonetheless, existing biomedical LLMs show limited comprehension of complex, domain-specific concept structures and the factual information encoded in biomedical Knowledge Graphs (KGs).

arxiv-2601-08779.title: Uniqueness for embeddings of nuclear C ∗ C^{*} -algebras into type II 1 factors Thanks: The first author was funded by the Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG, German Research Foundation) under Germany’s Excellence Strategy EXC 2044-390685587, Mathematics Münster: Dynamics–Geometry–Structure, by th
arxiv-2601-08779.creator: Shanshan Hua, Stuart White
arxiv-2601-08779.description: Abstract . Let A A be a separable, unital and exact C ∗ C^{*} -algebra satisfying the universal coefficient theorem. We prove uniqueness theorems up to unitary conjugacy for unital, full and nuclear maps from A A into ultraproducts of finite von Neumann factors: any two such maps agreeing on traces and total K K -theory are unitarily equivalent.

arxiv-2601-14688.title: Closed-Form Statistical Relations Between Projected Separation, Semimajor Axis, Companion Mass, and Host Acceleration
arxiv-2601-14688.creator: Timothy D. Brandt 1
arxiv-2601-14688.description: Abstract I derive the statistical relationship between a radial velocity or astrometric acceleration (a trend), a companion’s mass, and the projected separation of the companion. These relationships, expressed as probability density functions, are analytic and independent of all Keplerian orbital elements so long as orbits are randomly oriented in space.

arxiv-2602-17079.title: Environmental policy in the context of complex systems: Statistical optimization and sensitivity analysis for ABMs
arxiv-2602-17079.creator: Dylan Munson, Arijit Dey, Simon Mak
arxiv-2602-17079.description: Abstract Coupled human-environment systems are increasingly being understood as complex adaptive systems (CAS), in which micro-level interactions between components lead to emergent behavior. Agent-based models (ABMs) hold great promise for environmental policy design by capturing such complex behavior, enabling a sophisticated understanding of potential interventions.

arxiv-2605-09017.title: Quantum algorithms for path and cycle containment problems
arxiv-2605-09017.creator: Arjan Cornelissen, Amin Shiraz Gilani, Subhasree Patro

pmc-10579506.title: Impact of clinical diagnosis of myocardial infarction in patients with elevated cardiac troponin
pmc-10579506.creator: Anton Gard, Bertil Lindahl, Tomasz Baron
pmc-10579506.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). ObjectiveType 2 myocardial infarction (MI) and myocardial injury are common conditions associated with an adverse prognosis. Physicians experience uncertainty how to distinguish these conditions, as well as how to manage and treat them.

pmc-12609869.title: Perinatal Outcomes in Mexican Women with a History of Myomectomy: A Retrospective Cohort Study
pmc-12609869.creator: Fela Vanesa Morales-Hernández, Jocelyn Andrea Almada-Balderrama, Andrea Alicia Olguín-Ortega, Pilar de Abiega-Franyutti, Enrique Reyes-Muñoz, Myrna Souraye Godines-Enriquez, Demetra Gabriela Socolov, Iuliana Ceausu, Elena Bernad
pmc-12609869.description: Background/Objectives: Myomectomy is the preferred treatment for women with uterine fibroids who desire to preserve their fertility. This study aimed to compare perinatal outcomes between Mexican women with and without a history of myomectomy, matched in a 1:2 ratio based on maternal age and parity.

pmc-12732239.title: Complementary Feeding and Risk of Choking: A Survey Among Parents and Primary Care Pediatricians in Emilia-Romagna, Northern Italy
pmc-12732239.creator: Lorenza Parini, Elisa Manieri, Elena Corinaldesi, Michele Torella, Paolo Bottau, Eleonora Laderchi, Dalila Periccioli, Alessandra Cavallo, Chiara Bontempo, Eleonora Battelli, Egidio Candela, Monica Fae, Cecilia Argentina, Marcello Lanari, Arianna Dondi
pmc-12732239.description: Background: Complementary feeding has traditionally relied on traditional spoon feeding (TSF), in which parents gradually introduce semi-solid foods under close supervision. More recently, Baby-Led Weaning (BLW) has become popular, promoting infant autonomy in handling solid foods. To address concerns regarding choking and nutritional adequacy, the Baby-Led Introduction to SolidS (BLISS) method was developed.

pmc-12994167.title: Lithosyntrophy: Obligate syntrophy in a phosphite-oxidizing, methanogenic culture
pmc-12994167.creator: Heidi S. Aronson, Matt E. Weaver, Ruiwen Hu, V. Celeste Lanclos, Jacob D. Rapp, Anthony T. Iavarone, Hans K. Carlson, John D. Coates
pmc-12994167.description: SignificanceDissimilatory phosphite-oxidizing microorganisms (DPOM) use phosphite as an energy source, producing phosphate. While the two previously isolated DPOM couple phosphite oxidation to carbon fixation via the Wood–Ljungdahl pathway, Candidatus Phosphitivorax anaerolimi Phox-21 instead performs lithosyntrophic metabolism, coupling DPO to proton reduction in obligate partnership with a hydrogenotrophic methanogen.

pmc-13457825.title: A safety-aware intake modeling framework for translating edible algal biomass into nutritional bioproducts
pmc-13457825.creator: Yu Wang, Garrett Roell, Rica Dela Cruz, Michaela Durďáková, Jessica Maruwan, Kexin Rong, Rachel Novotny, Monica Esquivel, Lynne Wilkens, Wei Wen Su, Tao Yan, Kacie Ho, Zhi-Yan Du
pmc-13457825.description: Edible algal biomass has emerged as a promising platform for nutritional bioproduct development, but its practical translation depends on compositional variability, intake feasibility, and safety constraints. Here, we integrated biochemical profiling, trace element screening, age-specific intake modeling, and community consumption context to evaluate commercially available and supplier-provided microalgal and seaweed products within realistic application boundaries.
